title: Terms of Art in Medicine and Law
text:
Professional fields rely on terms of art, words that carry a precise meaning inside a discipline yet seem ordinary to outsiders. A physician who describes a lesion as 'benign' is not expressing an opinion about the patient's character; the word signals that the growth is unlikely to spread. Such terminology allows specialists to communicate quickly, but it also creates a barrier that can leave patients confused.

Lawyers face the same difficulty with words like 'negligence', which describes a failure to meet a standard of care rather than carelessness in the everyday sense. Courts must therefore define such terms carefully, since a misunderstanding can change the outcome of a case. Clear explanation, rather than simplification, is what allows both professions to remain precise and accessible.

questions.text: According to the passage, what does the word 'benign' signal about a growth?
options: That it is unlikely to spread
That the patient is a good person
That it must be removed immediately
A failure to meet a standard of care

questions.text: Why might terms of art leave patients confused?
options: Because they are designed for quick communication among specialists, not for explaining to outsiders
Because physicians avoid speaking to patients
Because the words have no real meaning

questions.text: What does the author imply courts must do?
options: Simplify the law until no technical terms remain
Define key terms carefully, since misunderstandings can alter outcomes
Avoid using legal terminology in judgments

vocabulary.definition: not harmful or cancerous; unlikely to spread
failure to take reasonable care, resulting in harm
the set of specialised words used in a particular field

paragraph_translations: Áreas profissionais dependem de termos técnicos, palavras com um significado preciso dentro da disciplina, mas que parecem comuns para quem está de fora. Um médico que descreve uma lesão como 'benign' (benigna) não expressa uma opinião sobre o caráter do paciente; a palavra indica que o crescimento provavelmente não se espalhará. Essa terminologia permite que os especialistas se comuniquem rapidamente, mas também cria uma barreira que pode deixar os pacientes confusos.

Advogados enfrentam a mesma dificuldade com palavras como 'negligence' (negligência), que descreve a falha em cumprir um padrão de cuidado, e não o descuido no sentido cotidiano. Por isso, os tribunais devem definir esses termos com cuidado, já que um mal-entendido pode mudar o resultado de um caso. Explicações claras, e não simplificações, permitem que as duas profissões continuem precisas e acessíveis.
